text: At 65 minutes, Kingsmoor FC implemented a pressing trigger by raising their press intensity from 0.5 to 0.68, increasing directness to 0.65, and pushing their defensive line higher to 0.62 in a bid to chase the 2-3 deficit[#1187]. This tactical shift aimed to disrupt Westport Albion’s vertical, direct passing by reducing space and forcing higher turnovers; however, Kingsmoor’s PPDA improved only marginally from 8.8 to 7.9, and their turnovers doubled, indicating difficulty in sustaining effective pressure[#1187]. The increased directness aligned with Kingsmoor’s 4-4-2 wide, crossing style to accelerate transition attacks via flank overloads, but this came at the cost of reduced possession (57.6% to 51.6%) and diminished field tilt (67.9% to 65.3%)[#1187]. Consequently, the team’s xG dropped from 0.05 to 0 over 15 minutes, reflecting that the tactical change increased risk without generating improved attacking opportunities[#1187].
